fractionalCto.metaDescription: A fractional CTO is a senior technical leader who works with your startup part-time. What they do, what it costs, and when it makes sense to hire one.

toc.label: What does a fractional CTO do?
When does it NOT make sense?

definition.title: What is a fractional CTO?
definition.body: A fractional CTO is an experienced technical leader who works with your company part-time — typically 8 to 20 hours per month. Not a consultant who hands you a PDF with recommendations. Someone who makes real technical decisions, writes code when needed, and stays long enough to see results.

whatTheyDo.title: What does a fractional CTO do?
whatTheyDo.intro: It depends on where your company is, but it usually includes:

items.label: Technical strategy
items.body: Deciding what to build, with what technology, and in what order. Build vs. buy. Designing the architecture that will scale with your business.

items.label: Team leadership
items.body: Hiring engineers, structuring the team, establishing code review processes, deployment pipelines, and documentation. At early-stage companies this means building the founding team. At larger ones, it means leveling up what's already there.

items.label: Execution
items.body: A good fractional CTO doesn't just direct — they execute. They review pull requests, solve architecture problems, and get hands-on when the team needs real technical support.

items.label: Audit and technical debt
items.body: Assessing the state of the codebase, identifying risks, and prioritizing what to fix first to unblock the team.

cost.title: What does it cost?
body: A full-time CTO with real experience costs $250,000–$500,000/year in the US when you factor in salary, equity, benefits, and hiring costs.

A fractional CTO typically charges $3,000–$8,000/month depending on hours and scope. For a 5–50 person startup that needs technical leadership but can't justify a full-time executive, the math is obvious.

whenYes.title: When does it make sense?
items: You have a product in production but no clear technical direction
You're a technical founder who can't do everything anymore
You need to hire engineers but don't know how to evaluate candidates
Your codebase has become a liability and you need someone to diagnose it
You're raising capital and need your technical story to hold up

whenNo.title: When does it NOT make sense?
items: You need someone 40 hours a week — that's a full-time CTO
You want an advisor who opines without executing — that's a board advisor
You can't commit to at least 3 months

comparison.title: Fractional vs. interim vs. consultant

items.label: Fractional
items.body: Part-time, ongoing, embedded in your team. Makes decisions and executes.

items.label: Interim
items.body: Full-time but temporary. Covers a transition while you hire the permanent one.

items.label: Consultant
items.body: Project-based, defined deliverables. Less integrated, more transactional.

comparison.footer: A fractional CTO sits in between: more committed than a consultant, more flexible than an interim.

fractionalCto.ctaBody: Book a call — 30 minutes, no commitment.

faq.a: A fractional CTO is an experienced technical leader who works with your company part-time — typically 8 to 20 hours per month. They make real technical decisions, write code when needed, and stay long enough to see results.

faq.q: What does a fractional CTO do?
faq.a: Technical strategy (what to build, build vs. buy, architecture). Team leadership (hiring, processes, code review, deployments). Hands-on execution. Audit and technical debt prioritization.

faq.q: What does a fractional CTO cost?
faq.a: Typically $3,000–$8,000 per month depending on hours and scope. For comparison, a full-time CTO in the US costs $250,000–$500,000 per year once you include salary, equity, benefits, and hiring costs.

faq.q: When should I hire a fractional CTO?
faq.a: When you have a product in production but no clear technical direction, when you're a technical founder who can't do everything anymore, when you need to hire engineers but don't know how to evaluate them, when your codebase has become a liability, or when you're raising capital and need your technical story to hold up.

faq.q: When should I NOT hire a fractional CTO?
faq.a: If you need someone 40 hours a week (that's a full-time CTO), if you want an advisor who only opines without executing (that's a board advisor), or if you can't commit to at least 3 months.

faq.q: What's the difference between a fractional, interim, and consultant CTO?
faq.a: A fractional CTO is part-time, ongoing, and embedded in your team — they make decisions and execute. An interim CTO is full-time but temporary, covering a transition. A consultant is project-based with defined deliverables, less integrated and more transactional.
